findings.title: Terminal attempts always have receipts
findings.proposition: Require a non-null owner receipt for every terminal JJ attempt, including failed, cancelled, recovery-required and effect-unknown results.
findings.rationale: The research identifies successful effects with failed or absent native oplog writes; an independent terminal receipt is therefore necessary. SCS-003 explicitly requires a typed receipt on every terminal attempt, but the JJ result schema permits receipt_ref=null and only forces a receipt for successful mutations. Tighten the terminal-result constraint; do not require a native oplog entry to exist after a failed native write.
extraction_keys: failure atomicity and independent effect receipt
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

derivation.research_role: Research supplies independent-operation-receipt motivation only; no research output identifies the frozen schema contradiction.

exact_frozen_evidence.quote:
Every source-control mutation requires one current writer lease with repository/workspace/backend, holder,
  generation, epoch, expiry and reconciliation state; one expected native revision; Permissions and FileSafe
  decisions; and one idempotent command instance. HTTPS and SSH credentials are brokered as expiring,
  revocable, operation- or GoalRun-scoped leases. Async work uses ObservableWork and every terminal attempt
  emits a typed operation receipt even when the effect is unknown or recovery is required. The nineteen

derivation.scope: Established command_result attempts only: command_instance_id, owner_operation_id and before_revision already exist. Pre-attempt availability or command_error_record rejection is outside this result conditional; do not invent before identities.
derivation.independent_review: Evaluator-derived exception requested and accepted by the blind reviewer; zero direct research credit.

findings.title: Nominal reads may write
findings.proposition: Classify and fence all effects of nominal reads: snapshots, ref import, head reconciliation, secure-config migration, lazy object hydration, index rebuilds and unpublished operation-diff objects.
findings.rationale: Already required as an adapter safety obligation: the frozen read/navigation route grants no writer, transport or interop authority. Native --ignore-working-copy or an operation pin is not proof of inertness. Use a certified safe read, a disposable copy where appropriate, or a typed blocked/degraded result; do not add ambient authority or automatic reconciliation to a read. The supplied findings refine implementation tests but identify no promise that authorizes these side effects.
extraction_keys: Git reads can hydrate authenticate mutate
explicit import export guard still snapshots
read operation diff writes unpublished objects
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Strict read-only repository mode
findings.proposition: Offer repository browsing when the original native store is mounted strictly read-only.
findings.rationale: Frozen canon permits safe degraded reads and blocking unsupported layouts; it does not promise usable browsing from every physically read-only native store. Native migrations/index rebuilds/reconciliation explain why this is additional compatibility work.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Writer authority is stronger than native locks
findings.proposition: Retain one admitted writer across UI, CLI, watchers, fetch/import and external Git activity; native advisory locks and timeouts do not establish ownership.
findings.rationale: Already explicit in JJI-003/004 and SCS-003. Upstream lock-free concurrency, best-effort interprocess locks, watcher pauses and hook re-entry exceptions are evidence for qualification tests, not a reason to relax the existing lease/currentness contract. Bounded waits must preserve waiting/cancel/failure truth and may not expire into permission to write.
extraction_keys: bounded lock wait and typed contention
optimistic ref guard not workspace lock
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Expected operation is not native compare-and-swap
findings.proposition: Check the exact expected operation and immutable target under the writer lease, including after long fetches; --at-operation alone only chooses a native starting view.
findings.rationale: Already required by JJI-002/003. A native mutation at an old operation can fork or later reconcile rather than reject; the adapter must enforce the promised comparison. Open native fetch fixes are not shipped certification or an alternative authority mechanism.
extraction_keys: expected operation not native compare and swap
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Exact durable identity and operation-local selectors
findings.proposition: Keep repository, environment, workspace, mutable change, immutable commit, operation and operation-local selector identities separate across selection, caching and mutation.
findings.rationale: Already explicit in JJI-001/002, SCS context and captured-target rules. Display offsets, basename, root spelling, selected tab, short hashes or ephemeral graph indices cannot replace the admitted target. Path normalization is a representation detail, not native identity. Same-named workspaces and divergent twins are useful negative fixtures.
extraction_keys: clicked target versus selected target isolation

findings.title: Process failure and cancellation are not no-effect proof
findings.proposition: Report actual multi-stage effects, partial publication and checkout progress, retain warnings, and reconcile unknown effects before retrying after timeout or cancellation.
findings.rationale: Already required by the terminal vocabulary, before/after identity receipts and ObservableWork. A killed child, HTTP success, accepted dispatch or failed native exit cannot prove rollback. Known-applied errors can already carry an after revision and affected identities; the schema distinguishes known_applied from unknown. Do not invent a new unconditional all-or-nothing promise.
extraction_keys: process-tree cancellation and reap not effect proof
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Partial multi-file resolve
findings.proposition: Preserve earlier accepted resolutions when a later external merge tool fails, and report their native after-state rather than claiming the entire resolve did nothing.
findings.rationale: Already covered by native conflict reconciliation and actual terminal effect rules. Supplied current-native source commits a partially resolved tree before returning an error. This is a distinct command-specific test case; exact supported-version qualification is still required and default Diffedit3 is not a shipped merge profile.
extraction_keys: multi file resolve partial native effect
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Unknown auth retry effects
findings.proposition: Do not copy fail-prompt-retry credential flows unless the prior operation is proven safe to replay under the same command instance.
findings.rationale: Already required by no automatic retry on unknown effects and exact credential leases. Whole-command replay can duplicate local or remote effects. In-band wait versus failed-operation replay is constrained implementation work under that settled policy, not a new user decision.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Native versus sidecar crash boundary
findings.proposition: Keep native objects, refs, workspace files and sidecar metadata independently observable across partial failure; recover from inconsistent state without trusting a healthy-looking graph.
findings.rationale: Already covered by exact terminal receipts, native post-restore proof and complete backup closure. GitButler demonstrates that a graph can look correct while snapshot metadata is wrong, and native plus database writes are not one atomic transaction. Preserve those fixtures and distinguish authoritative from rebuildable state; do not import GitButler metadata schemas into PM.

findings.title: Native recovery has explicit scope
findings.proposition: Keep undo, inverse-one-operation, full-view restore, workspace path recovery and external-file recovery distinct; undo never reverses a remote push.
findings.rationale: Frozen JJI-005 already distinguishes native recovery from FileSafe and demands exact after-state proof, while JJI-008 includes workspace maps and dirty files. Native merge-operation limits, restore/abandon undo traps and workspace_store paths outside op views are qualification/recovery-scope evidence. Avoid the disproven claim that stale-workspace snapshots necessarily vanished without any trace.
extraction_keys: checkout before metadata with exact baseline

findings.title: Operation diff baseline safety
findings.proposition: Compare the correct recorded workspace or committed baseline when presenting an operation diff, excluding unrelated dirty work.
findings.rationale: The supplied GitButler evidence establishes wrong diff-baseline hazards, not a separate Jujutsu reverse-selected-operation capability. Exact revision-bound projections and recovery proof already require truthful before/after views; retain the qualification case without adding an unsupported action.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Named operation waypoints
findings.proposition: Let users name and revisit operation waypoints without creating artificial native history entries.
findings.rationale: Neutral backend checkpoints already exist; the added proposal is a human-named operation bookmark/annotation workflow rather than basic recovery-point creation. Upstream has discussed but not shipped user waypoints.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Grouped operation history and undo
findings.proposition: Group an intentional multi-command history edit for review and, where supported, one user-level undo.
findings.rationale: ObservableWork already reports multi-step actions, but native Jujutsu creates separate operations and does not provide an atomic batch-undo promise. A dependent queue stopping on failure is useful prior art; grouped display and grouped recovery need an additional explicit product contract.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Operation history navigation
findings.proposition: Add recent-operation and redo navigation with a virtualized operation timeline.
findings.rationale: The frozen owner promises a separate Operation Log plus undo/show/restore, but not a recent-operation menu or redo command. Virtualization is an implementation option for this additional navigation rather than a reason to duplicate SourceGraph.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Operation history filtering
findings.proposition: Add user-facing filtering of noisy operation history by action, time or meaningful milestone.
findings.rationale: Upstream opset/grouping requests reveal a useful feature but frozen canon only promises operation log/show/undo/restore, not a query language for operations.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Structured operation descriptions
findings.proposition: Attach structured application action descriptions and correlation metadata to operation-history presentation.
findings.rationale: Existing command receipts already supply exact identities; new editable labels or enriched operation descriptions are presentation metadata, not native operation IDs or an idempotency mechanism. Upstream custom-entry requests remain unshipped.

findings.title: History maintenance policy
findings.proposition: Choose whether PM merely diagnoses operation-history growth or offers user-approved pruning/garbage collection.
findings.rationale: The native operation log can grow through frequent snapshots. Frozen backup closure protects retained history and fences GC but does not select an automatic retention policy. Suppressing meaningful native history or shrinking it before backup changes recovery scope.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Stale workspace recovery
findings.proposition: Expose stale workspaces and saved/unpublished recovery operations without destructive refresh or guessing the newest operation.
findings.rationale: Already required by exact workspace reconstruction, unknown-effect handling and native recovery proof. Later supplied evidence corrects earlier claims: apparently lost edits can survive as hard-to-find native snapshots, and op integrate recovery may need ignore-working-copy. Retain saved operation/change identities and distinguish missing metadata from erased bytes.

findings.title: Workspace adoption and synchronization
findings.proposition: Support explicit adoption, rename/path repair and synchronization of existing native or Git workspaces where qualified.
findings.rationale: Create/open/switch/remove and explicit backend migration are promised, but adoption/synchronization proposals upstream remain unmerged and are not the same as those existing operations. This is optional scope and must never silently change workspace identities.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Workspace archival visibility
findings.proposition: Allow a workspace to be hidden or archived without removing its files or claiming it disappeared from native history.
findings.rationale: The supplied GitButler archive model is an optional visibility behavior. It does not establish PM workspace authority and is not promised by create/open/switch/remove.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Divergent change convergence
findings.proposition: Offer explicit convergence of multiple visible commits sharing one change identity.
findings.rationale: Exact commit selection and truthful divergence are already required. A guided native converge action is additional capability outside the frozen 31-command inventory, with version-specific heuristics and possible conflicts.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.rationale: These are concrete adjacent-product capabilities; the frozen owner lists new/describe/edit/split/squash/rebase/abandon/restore. Each new action needs its own admitted command and native semantic qualification; availability upstream is not a requirement.

findings.title: Persistent review marks
findings.proposition: Preserve reviewed markers and line-anchored notes across matching rewrites, with stale or orphaned status when correspondence is uncertain.
findings.rationale: General review/annotation surfaces exist, but the supplied proposal is automatic native rewrite-aware reconciliation of review state. No frozen promise was found for that correspondence algorithm; it is new review behavior with identity-sensitive failure modes.

findings.title: Machine-readable hunk selection
findings.proposition: Expose machine-readable partial-change specifications for agents and scripts through the existing adapter authority.
findings.rationale: GUI hunk actions are already accepted. The extra proposal is an automation format that lists and applies selected hunks with exact native bindings, without installing a second runtime or treating content hashes as authority.

findings.title: Hunk and editable diff safety
findings.proposition: Bind partial-edit selections and editable diff saves to both rendered sides, native conflict state, exact session/repository/revision, and complete matched selections.
findings.rationale: GUI hunk actions, exact mutation identities and native conflict proof are already promised. Content-only hunk hashes, row numbers and same-name path sets are not sufficient. Unsupported binary/type/rename cases must remain explicit; this is implementation validation of existing behavior, not an automatic mandate to support every upstream shape.

findings.title: Empty, absent and failed reads are distinct
findings.proposition: Never turn missing content, a failed native query, traversal omission or unsupported type into a valid empty file/list.
findings.rationale: Already required by typed conflicts, exact currentness and visibly partial/degraded projections. Diffedit3, jj-hunk, Tatami and JJ View supply distinct failure examples. Preserve deletion, unsupported and unavailable states through read and save; missing remote-query data is not proof that there are no remotes.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Diff text and metadata round-trip
findings.proposition: Preserve untouched source bytes, deletion state and file metadata through diff editors; saving unchanged text must not silently normalize line endings.
findings.rationale: This supports existing exact external-file protection and native after-state/conflict proof. The supplied static Diffedit3 path normalizes CRLF/lone-CR through its text model and recreates deleted files empty; it does not prove all executable bits are always lost. Do not adopt that lossy behavior as PM semantics.
extraction_keys: diff editor untouched EOL byte preservation
diff save deletion versus empty file

findings.title: Edited text line-ending policy
findings.proposition: Choose only the newline convention for genuinely newly inserted or replaced newline boundaries in mixed-ending edited text, preserving existing CRLF/LF/CR on ordinary Save.
findings.rationale: FileManager already requires preserve-on-save and separately permits optional paste normalization. Those are settled. The remaining optional policy concerns newly created newline boundaries in mixed-ending text; it must not normalize surviving existing boundaries or reopen ordinary Save behavior.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: External editor path confinement
findings.proposition: Protect output roots, links, ancestor directories and file identities so an admitted relative filename cannot write outside the authorized output tree.
findings.rationale: Already required by FileSafe protection of exact external effects and native identity fencing. The supplied no-race regular-to-symlink example is stronger than a generic traversal warning; native checkout protection does not constrain a separate editor. A failed external editor cannot undo its prior out-of-tree writes.
extraction_keys: external tool out of tree side effects

findings.title: Partial external editor writes
findings.proposition: Distinguish whole-request validation rejection from I/O failure after one or more external editor files were written.
findings.rationale: Already required by exact file-effect protection and terminal reconciliation. A mutex or path preflight is not a multi-file transaction. FileSafe and the adapter must preserve actual affected files and native import outcome without claiming tool cancel rolled back earlier writes.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: External diff and merge tool handoff
findings.proposition: Offer a managed external diff/merge tool session, including supported remote forwarding, with readiness, save, exit, cancel and cleanup tracked separately.
findings.rationale: Frozen Jujutsu promises diff and conflict workflows but does not require launching a third-party diff editor or a remote browser handoff. If adopted, native authority and exact conflict checks remain mandatory; a browser opening or tool exiting is not completed resolution.

findings.title: External editor stale sessions
findings.proposition: Reject late saves from a stale diff or merge session even when a replacement repository exposes identical relative filenames.
findings.rationale: Already required by exact native revision, workspace and conflict identity plus terminal reconciliation. Opening an editor after ending native resolve creates a later separate write requiring fresh admission. URI routing, temp-file cleanup and overlapping save deduplication do not replace those checks.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Bound reads before allocating
findings.proposition: Bound file reads, scan work and concurrent content fetches before allocating unbounded buffers, and preserve partial/error states.
findings.rationale: Already part of bounded safe reads and graph hydration rather than a new capability. A size test after read_to_string does not establish a memory bound; scanner errors and unsupported files must remain distinguishable. The evidence supplies qualification cases, not measured PM regressions.

findings.title: Credential architecture and custody already chosen
findings.proposition: Use the exact owner-brokered HTTPS/SSH credential paths, operation-scoped leases, authenticated IPC, typed waits/cancellation and safe helper progress; do not copy a competing raw askpass architecture.
findings.rationale: Already answered by Source Control: exact git-credential-puppet-master and pm-ssh helpers, known-host/no-forwarding decisions, peer/lease-validated IPC, non-secret refs, no ambient credential prompting and no raw credential-bearing environment in ordinary records. Foreground/background/headless behavior, helper packaging and late-reply rejection must fit this policy. Competitor askpass retries, password dialogs, fixed accept deadlines and silent fallback are comparison evidence, not open choices to re-ask.

findings.title: Secret logging and redaction
findings.proposition: Keep credential values out of debug logs, receipts, artifacts and ordinary GUI state, and retain only owner-approved non-secret references.
findings.rationale: Explicitly required in frozen Source Control and Jujutsu central bindings. GG source logs OK:<secret> in debug mode; that refutes blanket claims that askpass values never persist anywhere. Prompt text may also contain account/path data, so calling all prompt keys safe is unsupported. This is a qualification/redaction test, not a new product requirement.

findings.title: Credential storage alternatives conflict with owner policy
findings.proposition: Do not adopt an application-secret backend that may delegate to plaintext Git credential storage or silently replace configured secret material.
findings.rationale: The proposed GitButler debug/E2E backend is not its release askpass path and can route secrets to a plaintext store. Frozen canon already fixes custody and non-persistence boundaries; repo or debug configuration cannot authorize a different credential store. Delete-before-replace risk is a generic implementation caution, not an established PM defect.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: SSH host trust is a separate decision
findings.proposition: Preserve SSH confirmation/notification kinds and exact host-key trust decisions rather than accepting unknown host keys or displaying every request as a password field.
findings.rationale: Frozen SSH contract already binds a known-host decision and explicitly disallows ambient credential prompts. Competitor accept-new convenience defaults and lost SSH_ASKPASS_PROMPT hints do not justify reopening that trust policy. The supplied evidence does not prove every host-key prompt uses ask_permission semantics; do not generalize empty-answer acceptance to all SSH prompts.
findings.adjudication_scope: Frozen-canon comparison of supplied research; no native runtime certification.

findings.title: Null standard input does not prove no terminal
findings.proposition: Reject the claim that stdin=null and stderr=piped universally make Git/SSH unable to reach a terminal.
findings.rationale: Unsupported as a universal statement: tools may open a controlling terminal directly, and behavior differs by OS/helper. Supplied newer notes qualify this. PM must suppress ambient prompting and own process lifecycles by explicit policy rather than infer safety from redirected streams.

A loopback bind, Host/CORS filter, UUID socket name or path allowlist is not owner/process/lease authentication. Protocol-version checks are a means of enforcing current compatibility, not a mandate to add an HTTP service.

It does not choose in-process native library versus adapter-owned CLI versus private service. Embedders duplicate CLI semantics; vendor forks own extra protocol and upgrade work; no public upstream RPC is shipped.
